description:
Here is a 5-line summary of the conversation:

1. You requested that all board column icons render identically as an icon centered inside a circular background, fixing the inconsistency between "on hold" status icons and custom column icons.
2. Investigation found the divergence in `src/components/kanban/board/SprintBoardColumn.vue`, where status columns rendered a bare `<i>` icon while custom/kanban columns rendered a tiny 2px color dot.
3. The recommended solution unifies both into a single `w-5 h-5 rounded-full` badge: a tinted circle containing a centered icon (or a small centered dot when no icon is defined).
4. A status → semantic token map (`STATUS_BADGE_CLASSES`) and a `columnBadgeClass` computed were added so canonical sprint statuses reuse shared color tokens (e.g. `onhold → bg-warning/20 text-warning`) while custom columns apply their picked hex color inline.
5. The change was scoped to one file with no store/API impact; follow-up options (unifying the modals' color dots and sidebar pills) were noted but intentionally left out of scope.

history.summary:
Here is a 5-line summary of the conversation:

1. The task was to allow adding and removing sprint columns in the codx-junior kanban/sprint board.
2. I explored the codebase and found sprint columns came from a fixed `sprintColumns` getter that ignored `board.columns`.
3. I updated `src/store/kanban.js` so sprint columns persist on `board.columns` with `{ id, value, title, color }`, plus add/edit/remove/materialize actions.
4. I wired the UI in `SprintBoardView.vue` (New column button, canvas affordances, handlers) and `SprintBoardModals.vue` (id-based column dialog + gated delete action).
5. All new affordances are gated by props so the shared kanban board and the read-only virtual "No board" board stay unaffected.

# Conversation Summary

1. **Request:** Enable adding/removing columns on sprint boards, then refine the sprint column model to `title`, `color`, and `status` (defaulting to title), with card status migration when a column's status changes.
2. **Architecture:** Sprint columns are persisted on `board.columns`; the `sprintColumns` getter returns them (falling back to canonical task statuses for unedited/virtual boards), and sprint boards work by writing each task's `chat.status`.
3. **Store changes:** Added `defaultSprintColumns`/`sprintColumnStatus` helpers plus `materializeSprintColumns`, `addSprintColumn`, `updateSprintColumn` (migrates tasks on status change), and `removeSprintColumn` (migrates tasks on removal); also made `newSprintTask` default to the first column's status and round-tripped `status` in board export/import.
4. **UI changes:** `SprintBoardModals` gained an optional sprint-only Status field with duplicate validation and a gated Delete action; `SprintBoardView` wires the New column button and column events; `SprintBoardCanvas`/`SprintBoardColumn` switched their references from `value` to `status`.
5. **Outcome:** Five files modified (`kanban.js`, `SprintBoardModals.vue`, `SprintBoardView.vue`, `SprintBoardColumn.vue`, `SprintBoardCanvas.vue`), with kanban boards unaffected since all sprint affordances are opt-in via props.

1. **Added sprint column add/remove** — persisted sprint columns on `board.columns`, extended the `sprintColumns` getter, and added `addSprintColumn` / `updateSprintColumn` / `removeSprintColumn` store actions with task migration.
2. **Refined the column model** to `{ title, color, status }`, where `status` is the `chat.status` a column writes (falling back to the title) and cards follow the column when its status changes.
3. **Created `IconSelector.vue`** — a reusable, searchable Font Awesome picker with a grouped icon grid, free-text class input, and `v-model` support.
4. **Added the column `icon`** through the store (defaults, getter, materialize/add/update, export/import), the sprint-only Icon field in the column dialog, and the view handlers.
5. **Changed files**: `src/store/kanban.js`, `SprintBoardModals.vue`, `SprintBoardView.vue`, `SprintBoardColumn.vue`, `SprintBoardCanvas.vue` (modified) and `src/components/ui/IconSelector.vue` (new) — no changes needed to the column renderer, which already shows `column.icon`.
